Sleep and memory consolidation

Sleep supports memory consolidation (Smith et al., 2020; Doe & Roe, 2019a). Doe and Roe (2019b)
replicated this in adolescents. Müller (2018) found no effect in older adults, cf. the
review by García et al. (2021). Daytime naps (e.g., Walker, 2017) may help too.
An uncited claim with a year (in 2015) and a ratio (n = 2020) is not a citation.

References

Doe, A., & Roe, B. (2019a). Sleep spindles predict recall. Journal of Sleep Research, 28(2), e12345.

Doe, A., & Roe, B. (2019b). Sleep spindles in adolescents. Journal of Sleep Research, 28(5), e12399.

Garcia, M., Lopez, R., & Chen, Y. (2021). Memory and sleep: a review. Neuron, 109, 1-15. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2021.01.001

Muller, H. (2018). Sleep in old age. Sleep, 41(3).

Smith, J., Jones, K., & Lee, P. (2020). Sleep consolidates declarative memory. Nature Neuroscience, 23, 100-110.
